platform.scopeDesc: Platform administration sees the shell of the system: accounts, roles, workspaces, project metadata and the audit log. It does not see content — no issues, no comments, no attachments, not even in private projects. Passwords are never visible here either. Anyone who needs to look inside a project uses emergency access: it adds a visible membership, requires a reason, and is recorded in the audit log.
platform.usersDesc: Every account on the platform — across all workspaces.
platform.deactivateDesc: The account can no longer sign in and holds no permissions anywhere. Issues, comments and assignments stay as they are — nothing is deleted, and this can be undone at any time.
platform.projectsDesc: Every project on the platform, private ones included — metadata, never content.
platform.breakGlassDesc: This gives you full access to a project you were never invited to. It exists for the case where the project lead is unreachable and something needs changing urgently.
platform.breakGlassVisible: You will appear in the project's member list — visible to everyone working there.
platform.breakGlassLogged: The reason, the time and your name go into the audit log, and stay there.
platform.breakGlassLeave: To undo it, remove yourself from the project's member list.
platform.breakGlassReasonHint: Why is this access needed now? At least 10 characters.

customFields.archivedDesc: An archived field is not on any issue any more, but keeps its answers. Restore it to bring both back.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.headerSummary: {active} active · {revoked} revoked — personal access tokens that authenticate requests to the public REST API.
apiKeys.expiresInDays: Expires in {count, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
apiKeys.descWorkspacesRead: Read the workspaces you belong to.
apiKeys.descMembersRead: Read the members of workspaces and projects you belong to.
apiKeys.createdDesc: This is the only time it will be shown in full — you won't be able to see it again.
apiKeys.revokeDesc: Any integration using this key immediately loses access. This cannot be undone.
apiKeys.baseUrlDesc: Every route in this API is relative to it.
apiKeys.authHeaderDesc: Send the key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
apiKeys.docsDesc: Every endpoint checks the token's scope first, then the same permissions your own account has — a key can never reach further than you can.
apiKeys.docsWebhookDesc: Not a request you make — an outbound push. Registered under Settings → Webhooks, sent as a signed HTTP POST whenever a subscribed event happens.
apiKeys.docsErrorsDesc: The same shape on every endpoint — check `error.code` when the status isn't 2xx.
apiKeys.docsErr401: Missing, invalid, revoked, or expired token.
apiKeys.docsErr403: The token doesn't carry the scope this route requires.
apiKeys.docsErr404: The resource doesn't exist, or you can't see it — deliberately indistinguishable, so a missing permission never confirms something exists.
apiKeys.docsErr422: The request body is missing or malformed.
apiKeys.docsErr429: The key's per-minute budget is used up — check Retry-After.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.headerSummary: Connect an AI assistant to this workspace over the Model Context Protocol — the same personal API keys and scopes as the REST API.
mcp.serverUrlDesc: The MCP endpoint every client connects to.
mcp.authDesc: Either a personal API key as a Bearer token, or OAuth — Claude's and most other MCP clients' connector picker discovers the OAuth flow automatically from this URL, no key to copy.
mcp.setupDesc: Pick your client. A connector-based client (Claude.ai, Claude Desktop) just needs the server URL — it discovers OAuth automatically and shows a consent screen. Everything else needs a personal API key, with at least the scopes for the tools you want to use.
mcp.setupClaudeCodeIntro: Add the server with the CLI — swap in your own key:
mcp.setupDirectIntro: Clients that support HTTP servers with custom headers natively (Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, and Claude Code's own `.mcp.json`) can point straight at the endpoint:
mcp.setupDesktopIntro: Add a custom connector with just the server URL below — Claude discovers the OAuth flow on its own and opens a consent screen in your browser on first connect:
mcp.toolsDesc: One tool per REST endpoint. Each still checks its own scope and your normal permissions, so a tool can never reach further than the key it runs with.

problem.dependency-cycle: Is part of a dependency cycle: {members}.

blocked.invalid: Its files could not be checked.
blocked.unsigned-not-allowed: It comes from no store, and plugins from no store are not allowed.
blocked.unsigned-code: It comes from no store and has code. Code from no store does not run in the app.
blocked.store-not-active: It has code and comes from a store that is switched off.
blocked.not-approved: Its code is not approved, so it does not run.
blocked.approval-outdated: Its code was approved for other files, so it does not run until this version is approved.

approval.approved: Code approved for exactly these files.
approval.open: Its code is not approved. It does not run until you approve it.
approval.outdated: Approved for other files, before an update. It does not run until you approve this version.

refused.invalid: Its code cannot be approved: its files could not be checked.
refused.unsigned-not-allowed: Its code cannot be approved: plugins from no store are not allowed.
refused.unsigned-code: Its code can never be approved: it comes from no store.
refused.store-not-active: Its code cannot be approved while its store is switched off.

pluginsAdmin.installBlocked: Plugins from no store are not allowed, so nothing can be installed from the plugin directory. Allow them under Plugin stores first.
pluginsAdmin.approveAsks: It asks to be allowed to:
pluginsAdmin.approveAsksNone: It asks for nothing in particular.
pluginsAdmin.approveAsksNote: What a plugin asks for is a promise, not a limit: its code can do more than it says.
pluginsAdmin.approveWarnTitle: You are letting this code run in the app
pluginsAdmin.approveWarnBody: After this, the plugin's code runs with the full power of the app: it can read the data of every workspace and act as any user, and nothing stops it.
pluginsAdmin.approveWarnFiles: The approval is for exactly these files. An update is not covered and has to be approved on its own.
pluginsAdmin.approveCheck: I understand this and I trust the authors of this plugin
pluginsAdmin.withdrawDesc: Its code stops running from the next request. What it already started keeps running until the app restarts. The workspaces keep their settings.
pluginsAdmin.installCode: It has code, and code from no store does not run in the app. Only what its manifest describes is used.
pluginsAdmin.updateApprovalGone: Its code approval is withdrawn: the new files are not covered by it.
pluginsAdmin.rollbackDesc: The plugin returns to {version}. Its files are checked against the ones that were replaced, and nothing that has changed since is brought back. The code approval does not come back: if it has code, that code stays off until the files are approved again. The version that is installed now stays on disk, so you can return to it the same way.
pluginsAdmin.uninstallDesc: The plugin is removed and the workspaces lose their settings for it. Its files stay in the plugin directory. If it is running, its uninstall hook runs.
pluginsAdmin.switchOffDesc: It stops running for every workspace. What the workspaces set for it stays.

pluginStore.title: Plugin Store
pluginStore.heroText: Integrations and automations you connect in seconds.
pluginStore.noResultsCategory: There are no plugins in this category.
pluginStore.noInstalled: Nothing from the stores is installed yet.
pluginStore.noStores: No store is switched on. Switch one on under Plugin stores to see plugins here.
pluginStore.noEntries: The stores that are on have no plugins yet.
pluginStore.storeProblems: {count, plural, one {# entry in {store} cannot be used} other {# entries in {store} cannot be used}}
pluginStore.incompatibleNote: This plugin does not work with this Barynt (it needs {range}).
pluginStore.revokedNote: The store withdrew the current version of this plugin, so it cannot be installed.
pluginStore.capabilitiesNone: It asks for nothing in particular.
pluginStore.capabilitiesNote: What a plugin asks for is a promise, not a limit: its code can do more than it says.
pluginStore.curationOn: Workspace and project admins see this plugin in their store.
pluginStore.curationOff: Workspace and project admins do not see this plugin.
pluginStore.curationInactive: Not used at the moment: workspaces and projects see everything from the stores that are on.
pluginStore.installCodeNote: It has code. It is installed, but its code only runs after you approve it on the plugins page.
pluginStore.installNoCodeNote: It has no code. What its manifest describes is available as soon as it is switched on.
pluginStore.installWarnBody: Installing takes the files from the store and puts them on this instance. It does not switch the plugin on anywhere.
pluginStore.installCheck: I have read what it asks for and want to install it
pluginStore.updateAddedNone: It asks for nothing more than the installed version did.
pluginStore.updateCodeNote: It has code. The approval of the installed files does not carry over: the new files have to be approved on the plugins page before their code runs.
pluginStore.updateNoCodeNote: It has no code. What its manifest describes changes as soon as it is updated.
pluginStore.updateBackNote: The files of the installed version stay where they are, so you can go back to it on the plugins page.
pluginStore.updateWarnBody: The update takes the files from {store} and replaces the installed version. Where the plugin is switched on does not change.
pluginStore.updateCheck: I have read what the new version asks for and want to update
pluginStore.syncFailed: {store} could not be updated. Showing what was fetched {time}.
pluginStore.syncFailedNothing: {store} could not be updated, so there is nothing to show from it yet.

pluginStores.title: Plugin stores
pluginStores.urlHint: The https:// address of a Git repository, without credentials or a port.
pluginStores.trustBody: Whoever publishes to a store decides what its plugins do. A plugin with code from this store can be approved to run with the full power of this app: it can read the data of every workspace and act as any user.
pluginStores.trustNothingRuns: Connecting a store approves nothing by itself. Every plugin with code still needs your approval.
pluginStores.trustCheck: I trust the authors of this store
pluginStores.switchOffDesc: Plugins from this store stay installed, but their code stops running until the store is switched on again.
pluginStores.removeDesc: Plugins installed from this store stay installed, but their code stops running.
pluginStores.noneOn: No store is on, so no plugin with code can run.
pluginStores.privateHint: Only needed if the repository is not public. The token is stored encrypted, is never shown again, and is only ever sent to this store's address.
pluginStores.tokenStoredPlaceholder: Stored. Enter a new token to replace it
pluginStores.usernameHint: Only if the host asks for one, for example Bitbucket or Azure DevOps.
pluginStores.accessDescSet: Set up an access token for a private repository.
pluginStores.accessDescChange: A token is stored. It is never shown; enter a new one to replace it, or remove it.
pluginStores.accessNote: Stored encrypted, never shown again, and only sent to this store's address.
pluginStores.unsignedDesc: Plugins that come from no store can be installed and used. Nobody has reviewed or tested them, so you use them at your own risk. For now only such a plugin without code runs; one with code stays blocked.
pluginStores.unsignedWarnBody: An unsigned plugin comes from no store. Nobody has reviewed or tested it before: not the Barynt project and not a store's maintainers.
pluginStores.unsignedWarnRisk: A plugin like this can be faulty or malicious, and it can put your users and their data at risk. You alone are responsible for what you install.
pluginStores.unsignedWarnEach: You will be warned again each time you install one this way. Switching this on is not consent for all of them.
pluginStores.unsignedWarnCheck: I understand that unsigned plugins are untested and that I use them at my own risk
pluginStores.unsignedOffDesc: Plugins that come from no store stay installed, but they are no longer loaded until you allow them again.
pluginStores.footnote: Only plain https:// addresses can be connected for now. Private repositories work with an access token; SSH keys are not supported yet.
pluginStores.visibilityWorkspacesDesc: Workspace admins can add plugins from the stores that are on, without asking you.
pluginStores.visibilityProjectsDesc: Project admins can add plugins from the stores that are on, without asking you.
pluginStores.curatedOnlyDesc: In workspaces and projects the store lists only the plugins you released for them. You release a plugin in the store, on its details.
pluginStores.curatedOnlyOff: Only applies where the store is shown.
pluginStores.visibilityNote: Approving a plugin's code stays with you, whatever is set here: a plugin with code that someone adds waits for your approval before it runs.

webhooks.deleteDesc: This endpoint stops receiving events immediately. This cannot be undone.

action.pluginProjectEnabled: Plugin switched on in a project
action.pluginProjectDisabled: Plugin switched off in a project

dashboard.scopeMineHint: This dashboard shows only your own tasks.
dashboard.workHint: How many issues and comments were created — counted, never read.
dashboard.growthHint: New workspaces, projects and accounts in the selected range.
dashboard.loginsHint: From the audit log. Failed attempts are highlighted against them.
dashboard.largestHint: Measured by their issues — where the load sits.
dashboard.customizeHint: Turn cards off or move them around. This applies to your view of this project only.
dashboard.statusHint: Every issue in this project, by the column it sits in.
dashboard.flowHint: What came in and what went out. A backlog grows wherever blue outruns green.
dashboard.priorityHint: Open issues only — what is done was urgent once.
dashboard.workloadHint: Open issues per assignee, unassigned ones included.
dashboard.attentionHint: Urgent, unassigned, or untouched for two weeks while in progress.
dashboard.attentionEmptyHint: No urgent issue is waiting and nothing has gone stale.
dashboard.noTeams: No team works on this project.
dashboard.noProjects: This workspace has no projects yet.

platformWorkspaces.desc: Every tenant on the platform — metadata and state, never content.
platformWorkspaces.suspendDesc: {members, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} will lose access. Nothing is deleted, and this can be undone at any time.
platformWorkspaces.deleteDesc: The workspace goes with everything inside it. There is no way back and no backup.

systemSettings.desc: Platform-wide behavior that applies to every workspace.
systemSettings.allowCreationDesc: When off, no one can start a new workspace — accounts without a membership join the default workspace instead.
systemSettings.defaultWorkspaceDesc: Where accounts without a membership land once workspace creation is off. Leave it unset and creation stays effectively on until one is chosen.

workspacePlugins.title: Plugins
workspacePlugins.intro: The platform installs plugins. Here you switch on the ones this workspace should use.
workspacePlugins.empty: The platform has not installed a plugin yet that a workspace can switch on.
workspacePlugins.cannotRun: It cannot run at the moment. {reason}
workspacePlugins.switchOffDesc: It stops in this workspace. What this workspace set for it stays, so switching it on again brings it back as it was.
workspacePlugins.unavailable: Plugins are not available on this instance.
workspacePlugins.platformNote: These apply everywhere. Only the platform switches them on or off.

blocker.platform-off: The platform has switched this plugin off.
blocker.needs-approval: It has code, and the platform has to approve the code before it can run.
blocker.approval-outdated: The platform approved the code of another version. This version has to be approved before it can run.

projectPlugins.title: Plugins
projectPlugins.intro: The platform installs plugins. Here you switch on the ones this project should use.
projectPlugins.empty: The platform has not installed a plugin yet that a project can switch on.
projectPlugins.cannotRun: It cannot run at the moment. {reason}
projectPlugins.switchOffDesc: It stops in this project. What this project set for it stays, so switching it on again brings it back as it was.
projectPlugins.unavailable: Plugins are not available on this instance.
projectPlugins.platformNote: These apply everywhere. Only the platform switches them on or off.

blocker.platform-off: The platform has switched this plugin off.
blocker.needs-approval: It has code, and the platform has to approve the code before it can run.
blocker.approval-outdated: The platform approved the code of another version. This version has to be approved before it can run.

workspaceStore.installCodeNote: It has code. It is added for the whole platform, and its code runs only after the platform has approved it. Until then it is added and not switched on here.
workspaceStore.installNoCodeNote: It has no code. What its manifest describes is available here as soon as it is added.
workspaceStore.installWarnBody: Adding takes the files from the store, puts them on this instance for the whole platform and switches the plugin on in this workspace.
workspaceStore.installCheck: I have read what it asks for and want to add it
workspaceStore.storeUnavailable: A store cannot be read or updated at the moment, so what is shown may be out of date.
workspaceStore.noStores: No plugin store is switched on, so there is nothing to add here yet.
workspaceStore.nothingReleased: The platform has not released a plugin for workspaces yet.

projectStore.installCodeNote: It has code. It is added for the whole platform, and its code runs only after the platform has approved it. Until then it is added and not switched on here.
projectStore.installNoCodeNote: It has no code. What its manifest describes is available here as soon as it is added.
projectStore.installWarnBody: Adding takes the files from the store, puts them on this instance for the whole platform and switches the plugin on in this project.
projectStore.installCheck: I have read what it asks for and want to add it
projectStore.storeUnavailable: A store cannot be read or updated at the moment, so what is shown may be out of date.
projectStore.noStores: No plugin store is switched on, so there is nothing to add here yet.
projectStore.nothingReleased: The platform has not released a plugin for projects yet.

pluginSettings.title: {name}: settings
pluginSettings.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved.
pluginSettings.tooLarge: The settings are too large together.
pluginSettings.overviewIntro: The settings of the plugins this workspace has switched on. What is set here applies to the whole workspace.
pluginSettings.empty: No plugin is switched on in this workspace yet.
pluginSettings.projectListIntro: These plugins are set for each project. Choose a plugin to pick the project.
pluginSettings.chooseProject: Choose the project whose settings you want to change.
pluginSettings.emptyProjects: No plugin is switched on in your projects yet.
